findings.evidence: The matrix proof references `h` only in `rw [DynkinType.cartanMatrix_apply_same, h.apply_self]`; line 367 introduces the extra root-system assumptions solely to call `isFiniteType_cartanMatrix`.
findings.fix: Prove the matrix result from a diagonal hypothesis `∀ i, A i i = 2`, derive any finite-type convenience specialization from it, and prove the root-pairing theorem directly using `Base.cartanMatrix_apply_same`, leaving only the ambient crystallographic assumption.
findings.issue: `existsUnique_dynkinType_of_card_eq_one` assumes full `IsFiniteType A`, but uses only `h.apply_self`, i.e. `∀ i, A i i = 2`; the root-pairing specialization at line 363 consequently also unnecessarily assumes `[Finite ι] [CharZero R] [IsDomain R] [P.IsRootSystem]`.

findings.evidence: The proof uses `hb`, equivalence of the finite support with `Fin 2`, and `b.induction_on_cartanMatrix`; Mathlib declares that induction lemma with only `[P.IsReduced] [P.IsIrreducible]` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/CartanMatrix.lean:230`).
findings.fix: Remove these three typeclass assumptions from this theorem; retain them only on callers that need finite type.
findings.issue: `cartanMatrix_ne_zero_of_card_support_eq_two` unnecessarily assumes `[Finite ι] [CharZero R] [IsDomain R]`; its connectedness argument requires only reducedness, irreducibility, the base, and the two-element support hypothesis.

summary: Several public statements retain assumptions substantially stronger than their proofs require, especially in the rank-one case.
